items.item_text: Valid California Registered License without restriction
Certified Radiology Nurse (CRN)
American Heart Association (AHA) Basic Life Support (BLS) or UC Davis Health CPR
Breast Health Clinical Navigator (BHCN) Certification within 24 months of hire
Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)
1 year of Radiology RN or Navigator Experience
At least 2 years of clinical care coordination and/or navigation in breast health and/or radiology

The Breast Health Navigator (BHN) provides clinical care coordination for patients undergoing Mammography procedures/examinations. The BHN is an RN with advanced skills who is an expert in Radiology nursing utilizing their extensive knowledge of breast diseases to serve as a consistent care coordinator throughout the continuum of care. They are responsible for assessing the healthcare barriers and the physical, psychological, and social needs of the patient, providing them with educational, emotional, and social support. This role requires a dedicated person knowledgeable in the flow of events in the screening, diagnostic breast care, treatment, and survivorship setting of breast cancer.
10% - Nursing Process and Practice Advocacy
The BHN is an individual who is trained to navigate a patient through the processes of care, diagnosis and treatment process.
70% - Clinical Care Coordination and Navigation

The BHN reports to the Assistant Nurse Manager in Radiology and works closely with the Radiology leadership team to ensure delivery of appropriate and timely services to patients and other key stakeholders. The BHN has primary responsibility for day-to-day care coordination of care throughout the entire pre-, intra- and post-procedure interventions in order to assist with the fluid operations of the Mammography services. The BHN acts as a mentor, preceptor, and resource for other Clinical Nurses (CN 1, 2 & 3) as well as other staff members.
5% - Professional Development of Breast Health Knowledge and Education

The BHN, in conjunction with the radiology nursing leadership team, assists in procedure policy and procedure development and ongoing updates. This position also provides input to department leaders regarding workflows to enhance efficiency and patient care. Escalates clinical or personnel issues to AN 2 or Nurse Manager as appropriate.
15% - Maintains and assists with Quality Processes
Graduation from an accredited school of nursing.
American Heart Association (AHA) Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) within three months of hire
Demonstrated commitment to excellence in patient care.
Ability to read, write, speak, and understand the English language.
Ability to utilize medical terminology appropriately.
Knowledge of current trends in nursing.
Effective interpersonal skills.
Demonstrated accountability and professionalism.
Ability to adapt to change in a positive, professional and productive manner.
Knowledge of legal implications in clinical practice and documentation.
Knowledge of performance improvement and evidence-based practice.

Ability to assess, plan, implement and evaluate patient care, taking into consideration protective interventions, development (behavioral and physical) and physiological characteristics specific to the patients.
